newsitem.title: INDIA: India 96/97 industry growth seen slowing to 8 pct.
newsitem.headline: India 96/97 industry growth seen slowing to 8 pct.

text.p: Indian industrial growth will slow to 8 percent in the year ending March 1997, handicapped by falling demand, high borrowing costs and political uncertainty, business leaders said Sunday.
This compares with an official industrial growth target of 12 percent for the fiscal year, after the country notched 12.1 percent in 1995/96.

"Industry will grow at less than 10 percent in the current year. In fact we will be lucky to have 8 percent growth," V. Raghuraman, secretary general of Associated Chambers of Commerce (Assocham), told Reuters.
Overall industry growth was 6.4 percent between April and August compared with 13.2 percent in the same period last year.
Lack of domestic demand for output, rising inventories, infrastructure bottlenecks and political uncertainty would retard industrial growth, business leaders said.

"We are looking at an optimistic figure of 8 percent assuming that demand shortfall will improve due to actions of the government," Amit Mitra, secretary general of the Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry, told Reuters.
